tests.description: The curve is generated, non-empty, and respects its cut-off.
tests.key: dragonPoints › stops early when fraction is below 1

tests.description: Sides follow the sequence itself: each is the sum of the previous two.
tests.key: fibonacciTiling › grows each square as the sum of the previous two

tests.description: openLast is the incompleteness: the largest square is drawn as three sides.
tests.key: fibonacciTiling › keeps the largest square closed when openLast is false

tests.description: The tiling is normalised to the origin, so nothing sits at a negative offset.
tests.key: fibonacciTiling › normalises the tiling to the origin

tests.description: This is the geometry the design handoff exported, reproduced from the rule.
tests.key: fibonacciTiling › reproduces the handoff geometry for six squares

tests.description: Below two squares there is no tiling to build.
tests.key: fibonacciTiling › returns nothing for a count under two

tests.description: Iteration n replaces each segment with four, so 4^n moves.
tests.key: kochPoints › produces four segments per segment per iteration

tests.description: Each pass rewrites every matching symbol.
tests.key: lsystem › applies the production rule once per iteration

tests.description: Symbols with no rule survive verbatim — the dragon's X and Y rely on this.
tests.key: lsystem › passes through symbols that have no rule

tests.description: Zero iterations is the axiom untouched.
tests.key: lsystem › returns the axiom unchanged for zero iterations

tests.description: A single dot is one unit wide and starts at the origin.
tests.key: morseLine › encodes a single dot at the origin

tests.description: A dash is three units wide — the classic proportion.
tests.key: morseLine › makes a dash three times a dot

tests.description: Letters are separated by three units, wider than the one-unit symbol gap.
tests.key: morseLine › separates letters by three units

tests.description: Words are separated by seven units, wider still.
tests.key: morseLine › separates words by seven units

tests.description: Unencodable characters are skipped rather than guessed at.
tests.key: morseLine › skips characters with no morse encoding

tests.description: Every symbol records the word it came from, for labelling and centring.
tests.key: morseLine › tags each symbol with its word

tests.description: Three sides only — down the left, across the bottom, back up the right.
tests.key: openRectPath › draws three sides and never closes the shape

tests.description: With neither override present (a real production build), the site reads its committed `src/content` — so deploys are unaffected.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › defaults to _projectRoot_/src/content when no override is present

tests.description: With no env var, the sidecar file the editor writes is the load-bearing override for a PTY-launched dev server that didn't inherit the env.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › falls back to the .codeyam/tmp/content-root sidecar

tests.description: The env override wins outright — this is the programmatic-launch path where the editor injects the absolute sandbox content dir.
tests.key: resolveContentRoot › prefers the CODEYAM_CONTENT_ROOT env override

tests.description: The data root resolves with the same env → sidecar → default precedence as the content root, defaulting to committed `src/data` in production.
tests.key: resolveDataRoot › defaults to _projectRoot_/src/data when no override is present

tests.description: Different seeds diverge, so the seed is a real dial.
tests.key: seededRandom › produces a different sequence for a different seed

tests.description: Same seed, same sequence — this is what keeps the static build reproducible.
tests.key: seededRandom › produces the same sequence for the same seed

tests.description: Values stay in the unit interval, which the jitter maths assumes.
tests.key: seededRandom › stays within zero and one

tests.description: Whatever the step leaves over, the path lands exactly on its endpoint.
tests.key: sinePath › lands exactly on the end even when step does not divide the width

tests.description: A smaller step samples more finely and yields more points.
tests.key: sinePath › samples more densely with a smaller step

tests.description: The wave starts on its baseline: sin(0) is 0, so no vertical offset.
tests.key: sinePath › starts on the baseline

tests.description: fraction is the incompleteness dial — below 1 the wave stops short of the frame.
tests.key: sinePath › stops short of the full width when fraction is below 1

tests.description: A single point is a move with no line — the degenerate but valid case.
tests.key: toPath › emits only a moveto for one point

tests.description: An empty point list has no path to draw, and must not emit a bare "M".
tests.key: toPath › returns an empty string for no points

tests.description: Float noise is rounded so generated paths stay readable in devtools.
tests.key: toPath › rounds coordinates to two decimals

tests.description: The trunk is always walked, so the figure is never empty.
tests.key: treeSegments › always draws the trunk

tests.description: A different seed grows a visibly different tree.
tests.key: treeSegments › grows a different tree for a different seed

tests.description: With no chance of branching, only the trunk exists.
tests.key: treeSegments › grows no side branches when branchChance is zero

tests.description: Same seed, same tree — otherwise every build would redraw the artwork.
tests.key: treeSegments › is deterministic for a given seed

tests.description: The named bare limb carries no children — the deliberate missing piece.
tests.key: treeSegments › leaves the named limb bare

tests.description: Depth bounds the recursion, so a deeper tree is never smaller.
tests.key: treeSegments › never shrinks as depth increases

tests.description: Limbs taper as they divide, so the trunk reads heavier than its branches.
tests.key: treeSegments › tapers stroke width with depth

tests.description: Even at fraction zero at least one move is walked, so nothing renders empty.
tests.key: turtle › always walks at least one move

tests.description: Bookkeeping symbols carry no geometry and must not move the turtle.
tests.key: turtle › ignores symbols that are not moves or turns

tests.description: Forward moves advance along the heading; +x at heading zero.
tests.key: turtle › walks forward along its heading

tests.description: fraction stops the walk partway — this is what makes a fragment a fragment.
tests.key: turtle › walks only part of the moves when fraction is below 1
